newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bombing trial judge maintains gag order.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bombing trial judge maintains gag order.

text.p: The judge in the Oklahoma City bombing trial on Monday refused a request from more than 70 news organisations to rescind a sweeping gag order he has placed on the attorneys in the high-profile case.

"This case calls for a blanket bar on out-of-court comments because no lesser restriction would adequately protect against a substantial likelihood of prejudicing the proceedings," U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch said in an eight-page written order.

The judge said the "compelling interest is the protection of jurors from being influenced" by comments from the parties in the case. The Colorado-Oklahoma Trial Group and the Colorado-Oklahoma Print Media group had asked the court to vacate an April 16 order. In a rare Saturday session, on April 26, the judge heard arguments from attorneys.

The judge said it was necessary to maintain the gag order to prevent jurors, who are not being sequestered, from inadvertently hearing a news account based on information from the attorneys in the case.

Matsch said he would listen to any requests from attorneys who feel a specific need arises to respond publicly to a particular story that may affect the trial. McVeigh's attorney Stephen Jones had asked the court for a limited right to reply in some cases.
